tasks.short: Calculate delivery, fulfilment and inventory metrics for operational reporting.

steps.what: Export shipment, order and inventory records for the reporting period.
Match records and resolve missing dates, duplicates and reporting exclusions.
Calculate rates and inventory turns using agreed periods and denominators.
Check totals and investigate unexpected changes against source records.
Prepare the recurring summary with results, definitions and unresolved caveats.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration brings {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} records into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliation checks and an exception queue in {WORKFLOW}. Configured measures in {BI} calculate the metrics; a template publishes results and explicit data caveats to {DOCS}. People resolve ambiguous exclusions, while routine refreshes publish automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Definitions differed across teams, exports needed matching, and small reporting changes required scarce technical time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting functions handle the calculations. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to connect exports, implement checks and maintain report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Missing delivery confirmations, changed promises and inconsistent inventory valuations can make mathematically correct metrics misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether an apparent performance change reflects operations, data quality or a changed definition.

ambition.what: Daily selection of delivery exceptions for operational investigation

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to resolving data exceptions and explaining service changes. The analyst gains discretion to select investigations within agreed thresholds; operational decisions remain with their owners.

reach.task: Resolve missing shipment confirmations before reporting closes.
reach.learn: Shipment event capture, correction permissions and proof-of-delivery practices.

evidence.claim: Structured logistics metrics can use deterministic calculations, reconciliation checks and configured dashboards.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is a recurring report assembled from operational systems, with a spreadsheet joining records.
Existing {BI} functions can express the agreed measures, so custom calculation software is unnecessary.
The design uses operational aggregates and excludes individual worker rankings.
GDPR applies where records contain personal data. Access and retention follow the reporting purpose.
unknowns: Which metric definitions and exclusion rules are approved?
Can the customer retrieve stable order identifiers, promise dates and inventory values?
Which reconciliation controls and reporting functions already exist?
Do worker-linked data or national rules require employee consultation?
research_questions: Can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} reports supply the measures before a separate pipeline is built?
Which source totals can detect incomplete or duplicated extracts?
new_work: Review unmatched records and approve analytical corrections.
Maintain metric definitions when operational processes change.
Monitor failed refreshes, access permissions and reconciliation checks.

tasks.short: Find inventory reductions that preserve service and operational resilience.

steps.what: Retrieve stock, demand, replenishment and purchase commitment records.
Identify slow stock, excess cover, duplicate holdings and unusual replenishment quantities.
Estimate working capital release and service exposure under alternative stock policies.
Validate supplier constraints, demand changes and critical stock with the planner.
Select opportunities and document proposed changes, limits and rollback conditions.
Approve, amend or reject the inventory reduction proposal.

tasks.design: Connect {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} data to configured inventory views in {BI}. A deterministic scenario calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares stock policies under explicit demand and lead-time assumptions, then fills a proposal template in {DOCS}. The planner validates operational constraints and the supply chain manager approves changes before implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, supplier commitments and service assumptions sat in separate places. Rebuilding scenarios took time, while many constraints remained undocumented.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inventory analytics cover standard signals. AI-assisted coding makes custom joins, scenario calculations and proposal templates cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Lost sales, intermittent demand, supplier disruption and critical spares weaken historical estimates. Inventory reductions take time to reverse.
tasks.human_edge: Balance cash release against service promises, supplier reliability and the consequences of a shortage.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a limited stock-policy pilot with explicit service stop conditions

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing a few credible inventory changes with planners. They can propose pilot scope and stop conditions, while approval of stock-policy changes stays with the supply chain manager.

reach.task: Adjust replenishment proposals around production schedules and supplier constraints.
reach.learn: Minimum order quantities, scheduling dependencies and shortage escalation.

reach.task: Set service and working capital trade-offs for inventory pilots.
reach.learn: Service segmentation, shortage costs and risk limits.

evidence.claim: Stock coverage signals and inventory scenarios can use configured analytics and deterministic numerical calculations.
Historical demand alone cannot establish whether a proposed inventory reduction is operationally acceptable.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The baseline combines system records with spreadsheet analysis and planner discussions.
Standard excess-stock signals are configured before custom scenario code is added.
Scenario results are recommendations; they do not change orders or stock parameters.
The pilot uses product and location aggregates. GDPR applies if source records contain personal data.
unknowns: Are demand histories adjusted for stockouts, returns and product replacements?
Which products are critical regardless of observed consumption?
What service targets and pilot approval limits apply?
Which supplier commitments can actually be changed?
Are consultation requirements triggered under national rules?
research_questions: Which inventory signals can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} functions provide?
How sensitive are proposed reductions to demand shocks and longer replenishment times?
Can historical replay distinguish genuine excess from seasonal stock?
new_work: Review scenario assumptions and investigate false opportunity signals.
Maintain product criticality, service targets and supplier constraints.
Track approved pilots against service stop conditions and realised stock reductions.

tasks.short: Review distribution and inventory procedures for practical cost and service improvements.

steps.what: Read current procedures, previous reviews and recorded operational exceptions.
Compare cycle times, handling costs, errors and service outcomes across operations.
Observe work and ask staff about delays, workarounds and safety constraints.
Assess causes and compare feasible changes against cost, service and safety constraints.
Draft revised instructions and a pilot plan from the selected changes.

loop.input: Current procedure, selected changes, recorded constraints and approved document template.
loop.output: Draft procedure and pilot plan with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate document structure and source references; the analyst checks instructions, constraints and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per document; unresolved conflicts return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle headings and fixed fields, but varying procedural prose needs contextual rewriting.

steps.what: Agree pilot ownership and approve the proposed procedural change.
Record the decision, pilot actions, owners and review date.

tasks.design: Configure procedure ownership and version records in {DOCS}, and build comparable cost and service views in {BI} from {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}. The analyst combines these views with workplace observation; a bounded drafting loop prepares revised instructions from selected changes. Approval in {WORKFLOW} creates pilot actions in {PROJECT} and releases the approved procedure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure documents and operational results were disconnected. Observation notes, comparisons and revised instructions had to be assembled for each review.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of comparable performance views and approval flows. A bounded drafting loop can rewrite instructions from supplied evidence without deciding how work should change.
tasks.still_hard: Recorded timings rarely explain causation. Local workarounds, safety needs and staff acceptance can invalidate an apparently cheaper procedure.
tasks.human_edge: Observe what actually happens, hear staff concerns and judge whether a proposed change will work safely.

ambition.what: A small-site procedure pilot service with a measured baseline and scheduled outcome review

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding comparisons and paperwork, and more time observing work and testing changes. They can lead pilot design and outcome reviews; the operations manager retains approval of procedural changes.

reach.task: Run a procedure pilot with owners, milestones and outcome measures.
reach.learn: Pilot scope, change dependencies and benefit measurement.

reach.task: Control revised procedures and verify that changes preserve required controls.
reach.learn: Document control, evidence requirements and corrective-action methods.

evidence.claim: ORTEC provides route planning used in delivery operations, supporting configuration before custom optimisation.
Performance comparisons and procedure version workflows can use deterministic software; causal diagnosis still needs operational judgement.
The proposed drafting loop and build ranges are design estimates, not a documented logistics deployment.

assumptions: The baseline includes document review, spreadsheet comparisons and direct observation.
Existing route or inventory configuration is checked before building custom optimisation.
Drafting uses approved operational material and does not invent safety limits or mandatory controls.
GDPR applies to worker-linked observations. National rules may require employee consultation for changed working methods or monitoring.
The consultation range allows for a limited pilot; formal national processes can take longer.
unknowns: Which procedures, safety controls and consultation arrangements apply?
Are process timings available at a useful level without individual worker monitoring?
Who can approve a pilot and release a revised procedure?
Are sites sufficiently comparable for shared benchmarks?
research_questions: Which cost differences remain after adjusting for order mix and site constraints?
What evidence would distinguish a process bottleneck from missing or late event recording?
Which document checks reliably detect unsupported additions to drafted instructions?
new_work: Review generated instructions against selected changes and source material.
Maintain comparable process definitions and document versions.
Coordinate pilot feedback, consultation where applicable and outcome reviews.
Handle conflicting instructions and retire unsuccessful changes.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain logistics cost models and demand forecasts.

steps.what: Agree the planning question, horizon, decision use and acceptable error.
Assemble demand, shipment, rate and operating cost histories; investigate gaps.
Specify assumptions, cost drivers, forecast methods and treatment of exceptional periods.
Implement calculations and fit candidate models from the specification.
Backtest forecasts or reconcile costs; assess bias, sensitivity and failure conditions.
Accept a model version and its permitted planning uses.
Publish the accepted version, assumptions and results for planners.
Compare actual outcomes with estimates and flag models needing revision.

tasks.design: A versioned pipeline on the {DATA_PLATFORM} prepares records from {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}, then runs specified cost calculations and approved forecast families. Deterministic backtests, reconciliations and sensitivity runs feed {BI}; the analyst interprets them before a manager accepts a release. Configured release workflows publish assumptions and estimates to {DOCS}, with monitoring against later actuals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data preparation, formula maintenance and repeat validation consumed the time available for modelling. Local workbook versions made assumptions and changes difficult to trace.
tasks.enabler_now: Numerical methods and validation techniques already exist. AI-assisted coding makes repeatable pipelines, model templates and versioned releases cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: New products, changing demand, incomplete cost allocation and structural breaks require judgement. Better implementation does not make historical data representative.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a useful model, challenge its assumptions and explain when its estimates should not guide a decision.

ambition.what: An uncertainty-aware demand forecast for low-volume product families

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time on assumptions, validation and planning discussions. They gain authority to recommend model retirement and propose new forecasting coverage; model acceptance and purchasing decisions retain separate owners.

reach.task: Specify dependable interfaces and operating requirements for a recurring modelling pipeline.
reach.learn: Data contracts, versioning, failure recovery and access design.

reach.task: Translate forecast uncertainty into capacity and inventory choices.
reach.learn: Planning horizons, asymmetric error costs and decision thresholds.

evidence.claim: Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates, supporting contracted-rate checks within cost-model validation.
Numerical forecast fitting, backtesting and sensitivity calculations do not inherently require a generative model loop.
The proposed modelling service, time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not documented customer results.

assumptions: The baseline uses system extracts, spreadsheet models and documented assumptions.
The initial build covers a bounded cost model or forecast family, not unrestricted model invention.
Reusable numerical components implement specified methods; novel model structures still require analyst development.
Historical time cutoffs are preserved during backtesting to prevent use of future information.
Operational planning estimates do not automatically issue orders, alter staffing or evaluate workers.
GDPR applies to personal source data. Employee consultation depends on the use and national rules.
unknowns: Which models and validation controls already exist in {OPS_SYSTEM}?
How much usable demand and cost history is available?
Which cost allocations and contractual rate versions are authoritative?
Who accepts model releases and defines permitted uses?
Are employee-linked data or national consultation requirements involved?
research_questions: Can an existing configured forecast meet the planning need before custom numerical code is built?
Which simple baseline should each candidate model outperform?
How should forecasts for sparse demand express uncertainty and trigger abstention?
Which monitoring signals distinguish data failure from a genuine change in demand?
new_work: Review data exceptions and changes to model assumptions.
Maintain numerical templates, rate versions and validation baselines.
Investigate forecast drift and cost reconciliation failures.
Record release decisions, retire obsolete versions and explain uncertainty to planners.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling figures and maintaining workbooks toward testing operational choices and validating evidence. The analyst can lead investigation and pilot design, while managers retain authority over inventory policies, procedures and accepted planning models.
reach: Help production planners turn inventory scenarios into controlled replenishment trials.
Help quality managers connect revised procedures to measured operational outcomes.
Work with systems analysts to make logistics data and models dependable.
skills_to_grow: Inventory service trade-offs and pilot design
Forecast backtesting, uncertainty and model limitations
Data interfaces, version control and access governance
Clear recommendations and source-grounded procedure review
role.ambitious_version: Run a logistics decision service that combines trusted metrics, inventory pilots, procedure reviews and validated planning estimates, with named owners deciding which operational changes take effect.
